In this episode, we're previewing the release of an experimental new plugin called Compound Writing, which helps you write with AI the way that we do internally. It's inspired by Kieran Klassen's Compound Engineering, and it's built by one of our staff writers, Katie Parrott. She's our head of AI consulting, and she's been on the podcast a few times, and she's just an incredible interviewer. Speaker 1 | 00:31 - 00:35 So I'm really excited for you to hear Katie and Natalia chat. Speaker 2 | 00:49 - 01:07 Today we're talking to Katie Parrott, staff writer at Every. Katie, if if you've been following Every for a while now, will be very familiar to you. She's one of our all star writers and we're so excited to learn more about her writing process and her new plug in today. Speaker 3 | 01:08 - 01:11 Hi Katie, how are you? I'm good. How are you? Speaker 2 | 01:11 - 01:21 So good. I am so excited for this conversation. I am revealing myself as a Katie fangirl on on the podcast. Speaker 3 | 01:22 - 01:23 It's a it's a mutual fandom. Speaker 2 | 01:26 - 02:08 Thank you. Okay so Katie, almost exactly two years ago you wrote one of your most popular pieces for Every, and it was about how you had just been laid off and also maybe were in the middle of a mental health crisis, which you've written publicly about, and you decided to turn to ChatGPT as a career coach. But at the time you were also an AI skeptic, which might be crazy to think about now given some of the work that you're doing. But can you take us back to that period? What was going on in your career and in that moment in time that led you to turn to ChatTVT in the first place? Speaker 3 | 02:08 - 02:36 Yeah. So I had just been let go from a crypto firm where I was working as an editor in Ghostwriter for the team. And but I was feeling really lost, as you mentioned, you know, like I had, like, tried crypto. I had tried, you know, in house. Speaker 3 | 02:36 - 03:00 I had tried out of house. Like, I had tried all these different things. And I I felt like I was at the end of what I could do on my own, and I really needed an outside perspective.
